values.note: Single site $26 a night (FS page and recreation.gov 2026 and 2027 peak seasons); double site $50, group site $80 (up to 24 people). One RV with tow vehicle per single site; an extra vehicle is $8 a night where it fits on the spur. Day use $8 per vehicle per day or $40 a season.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/hiawatha/recreation/little-bay-de-noc-campground ('Seasons of Use May 15 - October 8'; 'This campground is currently closed for the season.'; last updated October 8, 2026), read 2026-10-25

hookups.source: RIDB catalog for 232002 (all 36 single sites and both group sites typed STANDARD NONELECTRIC / GROUP STANDARD NONELECTRIC, reservable and first-come alike), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 36 single-family sites (20 reservable, 16 first-come) plus 2 group sites; all back-in, rated for vehicles to 40 ft (21 sites) or 60 ft (15). One RV with tow vehicle per single site.

sites.source: RIDB catalog for 232002 (36 STANDARD NONELECTRIC: 20 reservable, 16 not; 2 GROUP STANDARD NONELECTRIC; Driveway Entry Back-In on all 36; Max Vehicle Length 40 or 60) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232002 ('multiple single-family sites and two large group sites, available for tent and RV camping'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Accessible vault toilets and drinking water. Day-use picnic area and open grassy area beside the swimming beach and boat ramp.

facilities.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232002 ('Accessible vault toilets and drinking water are also provided. A day-use picnic area is equipped with tables and grills ... The picnic area is also adjacent to the swimming beach and boat ramp.') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/hiawatha/recreation/little-bay-de-noc-campground ('Vault toilets are available at this site.' 'Potable water is available at this site.'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 20 single sites and both group sites are reservable on recreation.gov; 16 single sites are first-come, and the 2026 rate table opens with a first-come week (May 15-21) before the reservable peak season. No switching sites on arrival; a reserved site is held until noon the day after arrival. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out noon (rec.gov) or 11 a.m. (FS page).

booking.source: RIDB catalog for 232002 (reservable flag per site) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232002 (rules maxConsecutiveStay 14, minConsecutiveStay 1, minWeekendStay 0; notices 'No switching sites upon arrival', 'Reserved Sites will be held until checkout time (NOON) the day following your arrival date', 'Check OUT is at 12:00 PM Check IN is at 2:00 PM') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232002/rates ('First-come, First-served Season 2026-05-15 2026-05-21') + FS page (check-out 11 am), read 2026-10-25

note: Hiawatha NF campground on the shore of Little Bay de Noc at the north end of Lake Michigan, 8 mi from Rapid River via CR 513; the group area is screened from the other sites by oak, hemlock and hardwoods. Day-use picnic area beside the swimming beach and boat ramp; the bay is a noted walleye fishery, and the Hunter's Point paved ramp is under a mile from the entrance. --Claude
summary: FS page (updated Oct 8, 2026) + recreation.gov + RIDB: $26 single (confirmed) + $50 double/$80 group, season May 15 - Oct 8 (new; FS shows closed for the season now), no electric (confirmed from the catalog), 36 single + 2 group sites to 60 ft, all back-in (new), vault toilets + drinking water (confirmed), reservable on recreation.gov (confirmed) with 16 first-come sites (fcfs some_sites new), 14-night max (new). Concessionaire-run per recreation.gov's refund notice. Water/sewer false (derived 'no hookups') left: the catalog types no water/sewer on all but one site. No Hiawatha alert or order names the campground or CR 513. Note trimmed of field restatements.
flags: Phone: the entry has 906-474-6442 (Rapid River Ranger District); recreation.gov says 'For facility specific information, please call (906) 767-1111.'

Operator: recreation.gov's refund notice refers to 'the campground concessionaire', so it is concession-run on National Forest land (concessionaire not named); ownership stays federal. recreation.gov lists the organization as FS and is_commercially_managed false.

The recreation.gov rate table carries walk-in rows for 'OAKS-STANDARD NONELECTRIC' and 'TWIN SPRINGS-STANDARD ELECTRIC' ($26); the catalog has no electric site, so electric 0 was kept on the catalog. If a Twin Springs loop has electric walk-in sites, that would change hookups.electric.
